title: orbitopt SceneData v1.0
description: A 3D scene (bodies, orbits, trails, an optional scrubbable timeline) consumed by orbitopt's viewer (orbitopt.viz.pv_viewer / Mission Control) and independent of orbitopt's compute code. This is a stable, versioned data contract: a scene file that validates against this schema today will still validate against it in any future orbitopt release. Unknown top-level or body-level fields are permitted (forward-compatible 'foreign members', GeoJSON-style) -- adding a new OPTIONAL field is not a breaking change and does not require a schemaVersion bump; removing, renaming, or narrowing an existing field's type does, and gets a new schema file (scene-2.0.json, etc.) with `schemaVersion` distinguishing which one a document was written against.

schemaVersion.description: Which version of this schema the document was written against.

id.description: Stable slug identifying this scene, e.g. 'solar-system', 'goes-gto-geo'.

distanceUnit.description: Unit every position/orbit/trail coordinate and info-row distance is expressed in, e.g. 'AU' or 'km'. Not restricted to a fixed enum -- any unit a viewer/reader agrees on with the producer is valid.

centralBodyId.description: id of the body this scene's coordinates are centered on (e.g. 'sun', 'earth'), if any.

result.description: Tri-state over every report: failed if any failed, not_checked if any was not checked, passed only if all passed.

reports.description: The high-fidelity verification reports for this scene's trajectory, each a document of orbitopt's verification-report-1.0 schema (the same ones `orbitopt run` writes next to the scene).

verification.description: Optional: how this scene's trajectory was verified. Absent means no verification ran -- a viewer should say 'not checked', never imply success.

model.description: What produced the grid, e.g. a two-body Lambert screen.

totalDv.description: One row per tofDays entry, one value per departureMjd2000 entry; null where the solve did not converge.

porkchop.description: Optional: the launch-window screen the optimizer searched (a porkchop plot).

candidates.description: Optional: the distinct trajectories the optimizer found, best rank first, for comparison. Each carries its numbers, what happened to it at candidate selection and at the verification gate, and a screening-fidelity path. Only the exported candidate (if any) has a high-fidelity flight, named by `flownBodyId`.

kind.description: Free-form category label for this body (orbitopt's own exporters use 'sun', 'planet', 'moon', 'spacecraft', 'reference'). Not a closed enum: the reference renderer treats it as display metadata only, so third-party producers/consumers may define their own kinds.

radiusDisplay.description: Marker size in the viewer's display units (screen-relative, not physical radius) -- used for the point-marker fallback when `texture`/`radius` are absent, or a body's texture fails to load.

radiusExaggeration.description: Optional factor by which `radius` is drawn larger than the body's physical radius (1 or absent means true scale). Lets a viewer state plainly that sizes are not to scale instead of letting an exaggerated planet read as real geometry.

texture.description: Filename of a packaged texture image (see orbitopt.viz.scene_renderer's texture asset directory) to render this body as a real, textured 3D sphere instead of a flat point marker. Requires `radius` to also be set; a body with one but not the other falls back to the point marker.

radius.description: Physical sphere radius, in the document's `distanceUnit`, used together with `texture` to render a real 3D sphere. Not required to be true-to-scale (a producer may deliberately exaggerate it for visibility, as orbitopt's own solar-system exporter does) -- only that it's a real spatial length in scene coordinates, unlike `radiusDisplay`.

rotationPeriodHours.description: Sidereal axial rotation period in hours (one full 360-degree spin relative to the stars). Negative means retrograde (spins backward relative to its orbit, e.g. Venus, Uranus). Only has a visible effect on bodies also rendered as a real sphere (`texture`+`radius` set) -- a viewer with no concept of continuous/idle animation may simply ignore it.

orientationBasis.description: The body's real inertial orientation at timeline time 0, as a 3x3 row-major rotation matrix from its IAU body-fixed frame to the document's inertial frame. Its third column is the real spin axis (north pole). A renderer uses this to tilt the sphere to its true obliquity and spin it about that real axis (combined with `rotationPeriodHours`), rather than spinning about the frame's +Z. Optional; when absent the body spins about +Z (optionally offset by `rotationPhaseOffsetDeg`).

orbit.description: A static closed orbit polyline (the renderer connects the last point back to the first).

orbitDashed.description: Render the orbit polyline at reduced opacity (used for reference orbits, e.g. a GEO ring).

position.description: A fixed (non-animated) position. Mutually exclusive in practice with `trail`, though both are optional and independent.

times.description: Non-decreasing timeline coordinates, same unit as timeline.unitLabel. Two consecutive samples at the same time mark an instantaneous event -- an impulsive maneuver, exported as its pre-burn then its post-burn state (same position, different velocity). They split the trail into interpolation segments: a viewer never interpolates across one, so a burn's velocity jump is not smeared into the coast on either side.

positions.description: Position at each corresponding `times` entry -- same length as `times`. Display data for playback: producers may round it (orbitopt keeps 1 m for spacecraft), so it is not a source for metre-level error analysis -- use the verification reports for that.

velocities.description: Optional velocity at each corresponding `times` entry -- same length as `times`, in `distanceUnit` per timeline unit (e.g. km/day when timeline.unitLabel is 'days'). When present, a viewer can interpolate between samples with cubic Hermite instead of straight chords (within each interpolation segment -- see `times`). That matters for a sparsely sampled body used as a moving reference frame: a one-day chord of Earth's orbit misses the true arc by thousands of km, which swamps a low Earth orbit drawn relative to Earth.

searchIndex.description: Index in the optimizer's candidate list.

rank.description: Rank by cost among distinct candidates (0 = best).

selection.description: Candidate-selection status, e.g. 'selected' (short-listed for high-fidelity flight) or 'truncated' (distinct but beyond the short list).

verdict.description: Verification-gate verdict: 'accepted', 'degraded', 'rejected', 'not_evaluated', or null when the candidate never reached the gate.

verification.description: Tri-state verification result ('passed', 'failed', 'not_checked') of the candidate's high-fidelity flight, or null if it was not flown.

exported.description: True for the candidate this scene's mission trajectory is.

bestEffort.description: Exported although it did not pass verification.

lambertTotalDvMs.description: Patched-conic (Lambert) total delta-v the optimizer ranked by, m/s.

flownBodyId.description: Id of the body whose trail is this candidate's high-fidelity flight.

fidelity.description: Human-readable model the path comes from (e.g. two-body Lambert). Never a flown trajectory.

times.description: Timeline coordinates; may fall outside the timeline when the candidate departs on another date.

positions.description: Same length as `times`, scene frame and distanceUnit.

bodyPositions.description: Optional, keyed by body id: that body's position (scene frame, distanceUnit) at each `times` entry, same length as `times`, from the same ephemeris as `positions`. Lets a viewer show the path in a body-centered frame at the candidate's own dates, which may fall outside the body's trail.

referenceEpochEt.description: SPICE ephemeris seconds (TDB, seconds past J2000) that timeline time 0 corresponds to, if the timeline maps to a real calendar date.

phases.description: Optional named mission phases (e.g. parking orbit, cruise, Mars approach) as [start, end] spans in timeline units, in order, defined by the producer from the physics -- a viewer draws them, it does not infer them.

deltaV.description: Delta-v vector in m/s; only its direction is physically meaningful for display (viewers draw it at a display-chosen arrow length).
